name: novel_gene_below_threshold
mechanism: A resistance gene variant with 85% nucleotide identity to the closest database entry is submitted to AMR detection tools. Most tools apply a default minimum identity threshold of 90% (ResFinder, AMRFinderPlus, ABRicate). A gene at 85% identity is below this threshold and will not be reported — the tool outputs 'no resistance genes found' and the isolate is predicted susceptible. In reality, 85% identity at the nucleotide level often preserves the protein function (synonymous and conservative mutations), and the organism may be genuinely resistant. This failure mode is called 'database lag': novel alleles arise faster than databases can catalogue them. The threshold is a policy decision, not a biological one — lowering ResFinder's threshold to 80% (`-l 0.80`) will detect the gene. The synthetic challenge uses blaTEM-1 (canonical beta-lactamase; beta-lactam resistance) mutated to 85% identity using a deterministic seed. ResFinder at default threshold reports nothing. The protein-level identity is higher than the nucleotide identity because many of the 129 mutations are at degenerate codon positions.

known_behaviors.behavior: Reports no resistance genes. Exit 0. Output TSV contains no rows. No warning that a near-miss exists.
Reports blaTEM-1 variant at ~85% identity. Correctly identifies beta-lactam resistance.
Reports no resistance genes at default 90% identity threshold. Protein-based scoring may differ slightly from nucleotide identity.
Reports no hits at default 80% minimum identity threshold (slightly more permissive than ResFinder). May report the gene depending on version.
Strict mode: no hit. Loose mode: may detect as 'Loose' hit. Provides explicit tiered detection unlike ResFinder.

samples.description: Synthetic assembly containing a blaTEM-1 variant at 85% nucleotide identity — generated by introducing 129 point mutations (transversions at randomly selected positions) into the canonical blaTEM-1b CDS (PZ399241.1, 861 bp) using a deterministic seed

recipe.description: Introduce 129 point mutations (15% of 861 positions) into blaTEM-1b CDS using random.seed(42), flanked by 500 bp of random sequence. Produces a synthetic 1861 bp contig. Identity to canonical blaTEM-1: 85% at nucleotide level.
recipe.command:
python3 -c "
import random
random.seed(42)
blatem1 = ''
bases = list(blatem1)
n_mut = int(0.15 * len(bases))
positions = sorted(random.sample(range(3, len(bases)-3), n_mut))
alt = {'A':'T','T':'A','G':'C','C':'G'}
for pos in positions:
    bases[pos] = alt.get(bases[pos], bases[pos])
mutated = ''.join(bases)
flanking1 = ''.join(random.choices('ACGT', k=500))
flanking2 = ''.join(random.choices('ACGT', k=500))
contig = flanking1 + mutated + flanking2
with open('subject_assembly.fasta', 'w') as f:
    f.write('>synthetic_blatem1_85pct_identity\n')
    for i in range(0, len(contig), 60):
        f.write(contig[i:i+60] + '\n')
"

download.command: echo 'subject is recipe-based; run acquire.py to generate'

ground_truth.detection_threshold_breakpoint: Gene is detectable at --threshold 0.80 but missed at default --threshold 0.90

curation.notes: The 85% threshold is chosen to sit between AMRFinderPlus/ResFinder default (90%) and ABRicate default (80%), ensuring differential behavior across tools. Real novel alleles at 80-89% identity to catalogued genes have been reported in clinical surveillance. The transversion mutation approach (A↔T, G↔C) is the most conservative — it changes nucleotide identity without always disrupting the protein. The mechanism captures the core surveillance gap: database curation cannot keep pace with allele evolution.
